memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You will plant vineyards and cultivate them but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, because worms will eat them. You will have olive trees throughout your country but you will not use the oil, because the olives will drop off. You will have sons and daughters but you will not keep them, because they will go into captivity. Swarms of locusts will take over all your trees and the crops of your land." — Deut 28:39-42 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once more the theme of labour without reward returns — vineyards planted but never enjoyed, olive trees that drop their fruit, harvests devoured by worms and locusts. It is the picture of effort that comes to nothing, of good things slipping through the fingers just before they can be enjoyed. This was part of the covenant discipline God warned would follow if Israel forsook Him: even their toil would fail to satisfy.

There is a quiet spiritual lesson beneath these agricultural images. Anything we build apart from God is ultimately vulnerable, no matter how much effort we pour into it. We can labour for years to secure comfort, success, or security, only to watch it slip away like grapes eaten by worms. Nothing gathered apart from God is truly safe.

We do not read this as our covenant curse, but the warning against building a life without God still stands. Jesus told of a rich man who stored up great harvests for himself but was not "rich toward God," and lost it all in a night (Luke 12:20-21). Earthly harvests, however large, cannot finally hold our hope.

The gospel calls us to store up treasure that no locust can devour and no worm can destroy (Matt 6:19-20). In Christ, our labour in the Lord is never in vain, and our truest inheritance is kept safe in heaven, beyond the reach of loss. Build your life on Him, and your harvest is secure forever.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I pouring my efforts mainly into things that could slip away?
2. What would it mean to be "rich toward God" rather than only toward myself?
3. How can I store up treasure that cannot be lost?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from building my life on things that can slip away. Help me store up treasure in heaven and to be rich toward You, trusting that my labour in You is never in vain. Amen.
